record.title: Anthropic adds server-side message threads to its Claude API
record.summary: Anthropic’s Nov 2, 2026 platform release notes introduced beta message threads for the Claude Messages API and listed availability across Anthropic’s API and three managed cloud platforms. The official documentation says clients create a thread with the full conversation and continue it by sending only new messages plus the prior response ID; the service retains the conversation temporarily. Threads expire after five minutes without a request and are deleted within one hour after last use. Anthropic says this reduces repeated upload, validation and tokenization work, but reports no measured latency or cost results. The feature is not ZDR- or HIPAA-eligible and does not support compaction, context editing, token counting or message batches.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Anthropic’s Claude Platform release notes dated 2 November 2026 announced beta message threads for the Messages API across the Claude API, Anthropic-managed services on AWS and Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic documents a create/continue interface that stores a conversation server-side and lets later requests send only new messages and the previous response ID, while retaining the initial system prompt and tools.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Anthropic says threads can reduce request size and keep time to first token lower and steadier as conversations grow by avoiding repeated upload, validation and tokenization of the full history; it reports no measured latency, token or cost comparison in the inspected release notes or documentation.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The documentation says a thread expires five minutes after its last request and is deleted no more than one hour after last use; it is not ZDR- or HIPAA-eligible and does not support message batches, token counting, compaction, or most context editing.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected sources do not establish realized latency or cost savings, reliability under production load, or suitability for workflows that require zero data retention or unsupported context-management features.

evidence_gaps.description: No matched independent performance or reliability evaluation was located.
The documented retention, eligibility and unsupported-feature boundaries may rule out regulated or privacy-sensitive workloads.

brief.importance_rationale: If the documented behavior performs as intended, server-side thread state can reduce repeated request transfer and preprocessing in long agent loops, changing integration choices for some API workloads; the current record establishes a beta feature, not measured savings.
limitations: Message threads remain in beta and require the documented beta header.
No matched performance, token-usage or cost measurement was reported in the inspected sources.
Threads are temporary, append-only state; applications must retain their own conversation and replay path.
The feature is not ZDR- or HIPAA-eligible and does not support several context-management features.
brief.summary: Anthropic’s Nov 2, 2026 platform release notes introduced beta message threads for the Claude Messages API and listed availability across Anthropic’s API and three managed cloud platforms. The official documentation says clients create a thread with the full conversation and continue it by sending only new messages plus the prior response ID; the service retains the conversation temporarily. Threads expire after five minutes without a request and are deleted within one hour after last use. Anthropic says this reduces repeated upload, validation and tokenization work, but reports no measured latency or cost results. technical.claimed_result: Anthropic expects smaller requests and lower, steadier time to first token in long conversations because repeated history upload, validation and tokenization are reduced.
technical.demonstrated_result: Anthropic published beta release notes and documentation describing the request and retention behavior. No measured performance result was provided.
technical.mechanism: A create request sends full system, tools and messages; subsequent continue requests reference the previous response ID and send only new messages while the server reconstructs the stored conversation.
technical.regime: Claude Messages API and listed managed-cloud platforms; beta header required; temporary server-side thread state; not ZDR/HIPAA eligible.
technical.reproducibility: Public API documentation is available. Empirical performance, reliability and replay results have not been independently measured in this record.
technical.strongest_baseline: Full-history Messages API requests resend and reprocess the conversation on each turn, as described in Anthropic’s documentation; no matched measurements were reported.

brief.title: Anthropic adds server-side message threads to its Claude API
brief.why_it_matters: Long-running agents often resend growing histories, increasing request size and preprocessing work. Server-side thread state changes that API pattern and may lower time to first token, but its value depends on conversation length, caching, retention requirements and replay behavior; the release includes no matched measurement.
